text:
maria: Quick convo — saved-views UX for console. Question: should saved views be strictly route-scoped single-model pins (simpler) or allow multi-model compositions (flexible but complex)? Need to decide for telemetry, cost previews, and sharing.

sam: I assume "single-model pin" means 1 saved view = route + model version. Multi-model composition = list of model pins + per-model filters/routing.

maria: exactly. single = easy snapshot, predictable telemetry. composite = lens that can steer across models.

kevin: Infra POV: composite is doable but complicates attribution. Telemetry ingestion must tag saved_view_id + model_pin_id for each sampled request. Also sim for cost previews needs to consider fallback behavior.

jess: From UX/sharing perspective, teams sometimes want to compare multiple model candidates against the same route. Composite could help, but we must show what happens if you apply the view on a route that doesn't support some model archs.

sam: What about rollouts? If a composite view includes a canaried model and its fallback, how does console surface expected traffic split and cost?

kevin: We could show a blended simulation: per-model token estimates + blended cost based on chosen routing weights or observed distribution. But that will add noise to the UI.

maria: Proposal: saved view has a mode flag: "single" (default) or "composite" (opt-in). Default keeps things simple for most users.

jess: I like default single. For composite, make it an advanced flow with clear warnings about telemetry, quotas, and partial apply.

sam: Telemetry detail: saved views must carry sampling and tagging fields. When applied, every trace/event should include saved_view_id and model_pin ids so regressions can be scoped. Otherwise we lose signal when views map to multiple models.

kevin: API sketch (example as a JSON blob, but we store it as a string in the thread):

```json
{
  "id": "sv:2026:001",
  "scope": "route:orders/create",
  "mode": "composite",
  "model_pins": [
    {"model": "redwood/opt-8b-q4", "weight": 0.6},
    {"model": "redwood/opt-8b-fallback", "weight": 0.4}
  ],
  "filters": {"max_tokens": 256},
  "telemetry": {"sample_rate": 0.01, "tag": "checkout_experiment"},
  "snapshots": {"perf_baseline": "2026-03-19T12:00:00Z"}
}
```

kevin: Implementation notes: extend simulation infra (we already sample requests for quota/cost previews). The sim should accept a routing table and output per-model token counts plus blended metrics.

maria: Console UX: save modal defaults to radio: (o) Save for this route only (recommended)  ( ) Create multi-model lens. If user picks composite, show a compact diff view and an expanded cost/telemetry preview.

jess: Also show "partial apply" if one or more model_pins aren't compatible with target route (e.g., different model arch or not deployed in the route's region). UI should let users preview which pins will be active.

sam: Quotas and Dedicated pools: composite views could reference models on different Dedicated capacity pools. We need clear guidance on how token accounting and capacity reservations work when a single saved view can route to multiple pools. Ops will want predictable billing.

kevin: We should snapshot model-to-pool mapping at save time and surface a warning if pins span pools. Also, snapshot performance/cost baseline at save time so saved views are stable until refreshed. Show a "stale" badge if underlying model metrics diverge.

maria: Rollouts: support saved-view rollout API: {rollout_pct, start_time, fallback_view_id}. This allows canarying composite views and automatic fallback. Must produce console timeline events and audit logs.

jess: Add read-only share links and ACLs: owner / team / org. Also export/import for reproducibility across tenants.

sam: Telemetry tagging change for sampling: when a saved view is active, sampled traces include keys: saved_view_id, saved_view_mode, model_pin_ids, applied_route. That helps correlate quality regressions to view-level changes.

kevin: Migration: existing saved queries map to single-mode saved views by default. We'll add a migration helper to convert multi-model saved queries if any. Also plan DB migration to store snapshots and compatibility lists.

maria: Action list: 1) kevin: API proto + migration plan (ETA: tomorrow EOD) 2) jess + maria: console mock for save modal and partial-apply flow (ETA: 3 days) 3) sam + infra: telemetry tagging + sim extension (ETA: 1 week)

console-bot: heads-up: enabled staging flag saved_views.composite for internal QA (:white_check_mark:)

jess: I'll include a compact cost-breakdown card: per-pin tokens, per-pin cost, and blended estimate. Also surface uncertainty bands if rollout is in-flight.

kevin: One more infra concern: sampling rate for saved views should be bounded to prevent a single composite view from driving excessive telemetry. We'll add per-view caps and org-level quotas.

maria: Good catch. We'll document limits and recommended sampling rates in the save-flow tooltip.

sam: Sounds good. If we default to single-mode, most teams won't need the complexity but power users can opt in. That feels like a pragmatic tradeoff.

maria: Agreed. We'll present this in product sync with a short demo. Thanks all. :sparkles:

sam: :thumbsup:

jess: :+1:

kevin: ✅
